claims.statement: Under docker compose, each service loads its own env file (backend/.env, prefect-proxy/.env, ai-llm-service/.env, webapp/.env), and compose `environment:` entries override only container-networking variables (REDIS_HOST/PORT, PREFECT_PROXY_API_URL, LLM_SERVICE_API_URL, CELERY_* for the ai-llm service, PREFECT_API_URL for the proxy and Prefect workers), so the same variables set in the service .env are ignored under compose.

Compose runs two separate Redis instances: `redis` for the backend and Celery workers, and `redis-llm` for the ai-llm service, so REDIS_HOST/REDIS_PORT point at different servers in the backend and ai-llm containers.

docker/.env is read only by compose interpolation and controls image tags, host ports, the dev secrets host path and CLIENTDBT_ROOT_MOUNT; the client dbt root must be mounted at the same absolute path on host and container because paths are stored absolutely in Prefect deployments and the Django DB.
The dev compose file overrides DBHOST (Postgres on the host), DEV_SECRETS_DIR and USE_AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER=False for the backend, so development uses the file-based DevSecretsManager.

Backend settings read DJANGOSECRET (no default), DEBUG (only the literal True enables it), ALLOWED_HOSTS and CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (comma-separated, credentialed CORS with no wildcard), and the DB* variables for Postgres with no defaults; JWT lifetimes default to 30 minutes/7 days and the JWT signing key falls back to DJANGOSECRET.
ENVIRONMENT=production sets PRODUCTION and changes the auth cookie SameSite policy to Lax (None otherwise); it also tags Sentry events.

AWS clients are built per service from separate credential pairs (Secrets Manager, S3, SES) and raise a ValueError naming the missing pair when the service is first used; SES_SENDER_EMAIL is the From address for email; USE_AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER set to the literal True selects real Secrets Manager, otherwise the file-based dev secrets manager is used and requires DEV_SECRETS_DIR.

The backend reaches Prefect only through prefect-proxy via PREFECT_PROXY_API_URL (with PREFECT_HTTP_TIMEOUT), and passes the AIRBYTE_SERVER_* settings and AIRBYTE_USE_SSL to the proxy when creating Airbyte server blocks, so Airbyte host config must be reachable from Prefect workers too.

The default and EKS Prefect work pool names (PREFECT_WORKER_POOL_NAME, PREFECT_EKS_WORKER_POOL_NAME) are read by the Org queue-config defaults and a migration, so the names are persisted per org and the pool the workers poll must match them.

The Prefect and Airbyte notification webhook endpoints compare the X-Notification-Key header to PREFECT_NOTIFICATIONS_WEBHOOK_KEY and AIRBYTE_NOTIFICATIONS_WEBHOOK_KEY respectively; the Airbyte key is read by code but absent from the backend template.
CANVAS_LOCK, EDR_TTL and ESTIMATE_TIME_FOR_QUEUE_RUNS and DBADMINUSER/DBADMINPASSWORD appear in backend/.env.template but no os.getenv read of them exists in the backend Python code.

Schema-change detection timing variables are parsed through get_integer_env_var, which logs an error and falls back to the default on invalid or negative values; AUDIT_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS drives the purge_old_audit_logs command.

The backend calls ai-llm-service using LLM_SERVICE_API_URL (endpoint building raises if unset), an optional LLM_SERVICE_API_VER path segment, and sends LLM_SERVICE_API_KEY in the Authorization header, which the service compares against its own API_KEY and rejects with 401 on mismatch.

Chat-with-data models are chosen via optional CHAT_WITH_DATA_*_MODEL env overrides whose model id selects the provider; a user-selectable model is offered only if its provider key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY) is set, and these keys are not in the backend template.

The prefect-proxy reads PREFECT_API_URL for every Prefect call, plus PREFECT_API_TIMEOUT/RETRY/RETRY_DELAY and PREFECT_PROXY_GIT_BRANCH, and Sentry settings; its template spells the work pool variable PREFCT_WORK_POOL while the compose worker commands read PREFECT_WORK_POOL, so copying the template verbatim leaves workers on the default pool.

ai-llm-service requires KAAPI_BASE_URI at import of ai_platform_src.py (raising an HTTP 500 error if absent) and rejects every Kaapi callback with 401 when KAAPI_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset; callbacks are verified by HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp and body with a replay window; AI_LLM_SERVICE_PUBLIC_BASE is used to build the callback URLs sent to Kaapi.

ai-llm-service reads Celery broker/result backend and Redis host/port from env with localhost defaults, and OPENAI_API_KEY is passed into its LLM API jobs; PROJECT_ID is only consumed by the service's own docker-compose.yml.

Webapp NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables are baked into the client bundle at next build (Dockerfile.webapp declares them as build ARG/ENV), so changing them needs a rebuild; NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL falls back to a localhost backend address when unset.

The webapp's next.config.ts uses POSTHOG_PROXY_HOST and POSTHOG_PROXY_ASSETS_HOST for the /relay rewrites and wraps the build with Sentry (SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN for source-map upload, maps deleted after upload, /monitoring tunnel route); PostHog provider uses NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY/HOST/INGEST_HOST.
E2E_ADMIN_EMAIL, E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD and E2E_BASE_URL are used only by Playwright; E2E_BASE_URL redirects tests to a deployed instance instead of a local web server.
